column2: People are leaving Alexa for chat apps, because simple household jobs still break. So I built Agora plus: a household brain that remembers, asks first, and proves what it did.
Tell it once. Remember Mia is allergic to peanuts. It answers in milliseconds, with no model call, and hands back a receipt. Verified means the fact was read back from a file, on a server I run.
Ask what Mia is allergic to, and it answers straight from memory. My morning briefing leads with what matters most.
It keeps the shopping list, puts a name on each task, and speaks up when a reminder is due.
Bigger jobs get a plan first. Plan dinners for this week. Four steps, and nothing starts until I say yes. The model is never handed the approve button.

After my yes, four agents get to work. Agora leads, Scout researches, Planner organises, and Keeper checks the plan against household memory. Keeper's verdict: the grocery list is safe for Mia's peanut allergy.
Everything it knows sits in a household panel that I can read, edit, and delete.
Under the hood, every step is a real M C P tool call with secure account linking, so an Alexa plus add-on, or any other assistant, can share the same household brain.
Agora plus. It remembers, asks first, and proves it.
